walkthroughs.body_html: Pluto is the most famous dwarf planet. Others include Eris and Ceres. They orbit the Sun but haven't cleared their neighbourhood.
The asteroid belt sits between Mars and Jupiter. Millions of rocks — none big enough to be planets — orbit there.
Comets are dirty snowballs of ice and dust. When they near the Sun, they heat up and grow a glowing tail that always points away from the Sun.
